title: KoreLumina — Master OS - KoreLumina Reconstruction Plan — message 0

metadata.content:
Add this as the next governing amendment to the Repository Engineer's Genesis task before continuing beyond the current Milestone 30 baseline.
Repository Engineer — Genesis Cross-Source Correlation and Evolution Episode ContractObjectiveRefine Genesis before further Historical Replay implementation so KoreLumina history is not reconstructed as a repository-only timeline.KoreLumina evolved through interactions between:conversations;human direction;architectural documentation;implementation tasks;Git changes;Runtime behavior;tests;failures;corrections;visual validation;governance decisions;certifications.These sources must remain independently provenance-preserving while being capable of correlation into one historical reconstruction.The constitutional principle is:Separate evidence.
Correlated history.
Governed conclusions.Do not merge source evidence.Do not treat correlation as canonicalization.Do not delay repository Historical Replay until conversations become available.Current BaselineCurrent branch:feature/genesis-historical-replayCurrent pushed HEAD:8fa2356ae38d06d5cc500ef1c9177d36fa800de2
feat(genesis): add replay read workspace shellThirty Genesis milestones already exist.Preserve them.Do not restart Historical Replay.Before expanding replay further, amend the Historical Replay contract and introduce the minimum cross-source model necessary to prevent Genesis from becoming repository-centric.1. Historical ModelGenesis must distinguish four layers.Layer 1 — Source EvidenceImmutable or provenance-preserving observations from individual sources.Examples:Conversation Evidence
Documentation Evidence
Git Evidence
Runtime Evidence
Test Evidence
Mission Evidence
Certification Evidence
Human Validation EvidenceEach source retains its own identity and provenance.Layer 2 — Historical EventsA normalized representation that something happened.Examples:requirement stated
architecture proposed
decision approved
task delegated
implementation committed
build executed
test failed
visual validation failed
correction requested
replacement implemented
visual certification passed
document superseded
release certifiedA historical event must retain references to its source evidence.Layer 3 — Evolution EpisodesA governed historical correlation of related events describing the evolution of one concern, capability, decision, defect, architecture, or implementation.Example:Episode:
Production Workspace Surface Normalization

Conversation:

Certified implementationThe episode does not erase any failed or superseded step.Layer 4 — Governed KnowledgeOnly after historical reconstruction does knowledge enter the existing Knowledge Operations governance lifecycle where appropriate.Evolution Episode

Educational eligibilityHistorical reconstruction itself is not canonical promotion.2. Source IndependenceConversation and repository artifacts must remain separate evidence.For example:Conversation C-123
Commit abc123
Build B-456
Certification CERT-789must remain four independently traceable artifacts.Do not collapse them into one record.The episode contains references to them.This ensures Genesis can answer separately:What did the human request?What did the engineer implement?What did Git record?What did Runtime actually do?What did testing prove?What was visually accepted?What did governance approve?3. Conversation-to-Implementation RelationshipsGenesis must support relationships such as:requested
clarified

strong
probable
possible
unresolvedExamples:ExplicitA conversation/task directly references a commit, file, document, issue, or milestone.StrongNames, scope, chronology, changed files, and validation evidence strongly identify the relationship.ProbableEvidence suggests a relationship but does not establish it conclusively.PossibleTemporal/topic similarity exists but evidence is insufficient.UnresolvedConflicting evidence prevents reliable correlation.Do not promote possible into historical fact.5. Causality RuleChronology is not causality.This:Conversation at 10:00
Commit at 10:30does not automatically mean:Conversation caused CommitGenesis may represent:occurred_beforewithout representing:causedunless sufficient evidence exists.6. Failed Paths Are First-Class HistoryGenesis must preserve unsuccessful evolution.Example:Approach A proposed
→ Approach A implemented
→ build green
→ visual validation red
→ correction requested
→ Approach B implemented
→ build green
→ visual validation green
→ B acceptedDo not discard Approach A.Do not teach Approach A as current architecture.Instead preserve:historical_attempt
failed_validation
lesson
replacement
accepted_outcomeThis is essential for Chief Agent education.The Chief Agent should eventually be able to understand not only:What does KoreLumina do?but:Why does KoreLumina do it this way, what was tried before, what failed, and what evidence caused the current design to emerge?7. Current Truth vs Historical TruthEvery Evolution Episode must be capable of distinguishing:historically true
historically authoritative
historically proposed
historically rejected
historically implemented
historically validatedfrom:currently authoritative
currently implemented
currently superseded
currently retiredGenesis must not flatten historical authority into current authority.8. Conversation Source BoundaryHistorical conversations live outside the repository.Do not search Git for them.Do not substitute commit messages for conversations.Represent their current Genesis coverage as:EXTERNAL SOURCE — NOT YET INGESTEDThe architecture must nevertheless be capable of admitting conversation evidence later without changing the historical identity model.9. External Conversation AcquisitionDo not implement ChatGPT acquisition in this milestone unless an existing supported source mechanism is already present and governed.Define the boundary only.Future acquisition must preserve:conversation identity
message identity
project/conversation association
timestamp where available
speaker/role
ordering
source reference
import/acquisition event
integrity informationAcquisition and compilation remain separate:Conversation Source

Conversation Evidence

Conversation Compiler10. Episode IdentityEvolution Episodes require deterministic identity.Do not use random IDs where deterministic reconstruction is possible.Episode identity should be stable across replay when its defining historical evidence has not changed.The contract must define:episode identity;source membership;revision behavior;merge behavior;split behavior;supersession;replay idempotency.Do not allow replay to create duplicate historical episodes.11. Event IdentityHistorical Events also require stable identity.The same source observation replayed twice must resolve to the same event identity.Where the underlying source changes, preserve revision/lineage rather than silently replacing history.12. Episode LifecycleAt minimum evaluate a lifecycle equivalent to:candidate
correlating
correlated
conflicted
incomplete
validated
superseded
archivedDo not invent statuses merely for UI appearance.Use only states justified by the historical reconstruction contract.13. Conflicting EvidenceGenesis must expect sources to disagree.Example:Conversation:
"Feature is complete"

Git:
implementation exists

Later conversation:
"Didn't work"

Replacement commit:
fixes defect

Certification:
greenThe correct Genesis representation is not to choose the first or latest statement blindly.Preserve the conflict and its resolution sequence.14. Human Validation EvidenceUser validation is historically meaningful evidence.Examples:green
red
didn't work
visually certified
approved
proceedThese statements must retain their context.A bare historical "green" without the artifact/milestone it validated is not useful institutional knowledge.When conversation ingestion becomes available, correlate validation statements to the artifact or implementation under inspection where evidence permits.15. Documentation CorrelationDocumentation may participate in an Evolution Episode as:governed_by
specified_by
amended_by
reconciled_by
superseded_by
certified_byDocument authority must come from Constitutional Documentation Governance.Do not infer authority from chronology.16. Git CorrelationGit provides implementation evidence.Preserve:commit identity;parentage;timestamp;files affected;branch/tag context where relevant;commit message;source revision.Git proves what was committed.It does not independently prove:architectural correctness;human approval;visual certification;current authority.17. Runtime and Test CorrelationWhere available, Runtime and test evidence should answer:Did the implementation execute?
Did it pass?
Did it fail?
Was the failure recovered?
Did subsequent implementation replace it?Build success is not equivalent to UI certification.Test success is not equivalent to constitutional approval.Keep evidence types distinct.18. Certification CorrelationCertification records are high-value historical evidence.Genesis should correlate certification with the exact implementation/revision it certified.Avoid representing:Feature X was certifiedwithout identifying which revision/state received certification.19. Repository Historical Replay Must ContinueDo not wait for conversation acquisition.Continue:Repository Sources

Episode RevisionThe episode identity should remain stable where it represents the same historical evolution.Conversation enrichment should add:intent;rationale;human direction;rejected alternatives;corrections;validation context;without destroying existing repository provenance.23. UI Contract ImpactDo not redesign GenesisReplayReadWorkspace.tsx during this contract milestone.First establish the data/domain contract.Future Genesis UI should eventually support:source timeline;Evolution Episode timeline;source relationships;current vs historical authority;failed paths;corrections;supersession;external-context-pending indicators;correlation confidence;provenance;Knowledge Operations lifecycle;educational eligibility.Any UI extension remains subject to the existing rule:UI
→ polish

→ reusable Lumina extraction if justified

Required Implementation NowBefore continuing broad Historical Replay, implement only the minimum durable foundation necessary for cross-source reconstruction.At minimum establish:HistoricalSourceReferenceDomain-neutral reference to evidence origin.HistoricalEventStable normalized historical occurrence.HistoricalRelationshipTyped relationship between events/evidence.EvolutionEpisodeStable correlation container.CorrelationEvidenceWhy Genesis believes two historical records are related.CorrelationConfidenceExplicit confidence model.TemporalAuthorityHistorical versus current authority representation.Names may differ if equivalent existing contracts already exist.Prefer reconciliation over duplication.25. PersistencePersist historical correlation state through the existing Genesis storage boundary.Requirements:deterministic;replay-safe;test-isolated;production-isolated;recoverable;auditable;provenance-preserving.Do not store generated Genesis data in source-controlled directories unless architecture explicitly requires it.26. TestingAdd focused tests proving at minimum:source evidence retains independent identity;historical event identity is deterministic;episode identity is deterministic;replay does not duplicate events;replay does not duplicate episodes;one episode may contain multiple source types;correlation preserves source provenance;chronology does not automatically create causality;explicit correlation is distinguishable from inferred correlation;failed implementation remains in history after replacement;superseded evidence remains inspectable;current authority differs from historical authority;unresolved correlation remains unresolved;external conversation source can be represented without a repository path;external-context-pending does not block repository replay;test persistence cannot contaminate production Genesis data.27. Documentation AmendmentUpdate:docs/architecture/HISTORICAL_REPLAY_CONTRACT_V1.mdrather than creating a competing Genesis architecture document unless repository governance requires a separate amendment.Document:source independence;Historical Events;Evolution Episodes;correlation;confidence;causality restrictions;temporal authority;failed-path preservation;conversation external-source boundary;future enrichment behavior.Do not redefine the Knowledge Constitution.28.
